questions.questionTextEn: Select the word that is most similar in meaning to 'TENACIOUS':
questions.explanationEn: 'Tenacious' means holding firmly to a purpose or course of action, which is synonymous with 'persistent'.

questions.questionTextEn: If 12 technicians can assemble a detector array in 15 days, how many days will 20 technicians take working at the same rate?
questions.explanationEn: Total work = $12 \times 15 = 180$ technician-days. With 20 technicians, time = $180 / 20 = 9$ days.

questions.questionTextEn: In a certain code, 'PHOTON' is written as 'QIPUPO'. How is 'QUARK' written in that code?
questions.explanationEn: Each letter is shifted forward by +1: Q->R, U->V, A->B, R->S, K->L, giving 'RVBSL'.

questions.questionTextEn: Choose the word most nearly OPPOSITE in meaning to 'LUCID'.
questions.explanationEn: 'Lucid' means clearly expressed and easy to understand; its antonym is 'obscure'.

questions.questionTextEn: A circular sheet is folded in half twice (into a quadrant) and a straight diagonal cut is made snipping off the central corner tip (where the two fold lines meet). When unfolded, what shape is cut out from the center of the circle?
questions.explanationEn: Snipping the corner of the 4-layer quadrant symmetrically along a straight line produces 4 equal sides meeting at right angles — a square/diamond hole at the center.

questions.questionTextEn: In a 100 m race, A beats B by 10 m and B beats C by 10 m (running at constant speeds). By how many meters does A beat C?
questions.explanationEn: When A runs 100 m, B runs 90 m. When B runs 100 m, C runs 90 m, so when B runs 90 m, C runs $90 \times 0.9 = 81\text{ m}$. A beats C by $100 - 81 = 19\text{ m}$.

questions.questionTextEn: What is the unit digit of $3^{43} + 7^{29}$?
questions.explanationEn: Unit digits of powers of 3 cycle every 4: $3, 9, 7, 1$; $43 \equiv 3 \pmod 4 \implies 7$. Powers of 7 cycle: $7, 9, 3, 1$; $29 \equiv 1 \pmod 4 \implies 7$. Sum ends in $7 + 7 = 14 \implies 4$.

questions.questionTextEn: Two candles of equal height burn completely in 4 hours and 6 hours respectively at uniform rates. If both are lit simultaneously, after how many hours will one candle be exactly twice the height of the other?
questions.explanationEn: Remaining heights at time $t$: $1 - t/4$ and $1 - t/6$. Setting $1 - t/6 = 2(1 - t/4) \implies 1 - t/6 = 2 - t/2 \implies t/3 = 1 \implies t = 3$ hours.

questions.questionTextEn: From a committee of 5 physicists and 4 mathematicians, a 4-member panel is chosen at random. What is the probability that the panel has at least 3 physicists?
questions.explanationEn: Total ways = $\binom{9}{4} = 126$. Favorable: (3P, 1M) = $\binom{5}{3}\binom{4}{1} = 40$, plus (4P, 0M) = $\binom{5}{4} = 5$, total 45. Probability = $45/126 = 5/14$.

questions.questionTextEn: A vessel contains 60 L of a milk-water mixture in the ratio $3 : 1$. How many liters of water must be added to make the ratio $3 : 2$?
questions.explanationEn: Initially milk = 45 L and water = 15 L. For $45 : (15 + w) = 3 : 2$, we need $15 + w = 30 \implies w = 15\text{ L}$.

questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following functions $f(z)$ of a complex variable $z = x + iy$ is analytic EVERYWHERE in the complex plane (entire)?
questions.explanationEn: $e^{z^2}$ is a composition of entire functions and satisfies Cauchy-Riemann equations everywhere. $\bar{z}$ and $|z|^2$ are nowhere analytic, and $1/z$ has a pole at $z = 0$.

questions.questionTextEn: In the Hamilton-Jacobi formalism, the principal function $S(q, \alpha, t)$ satisfies which equation?
questions.explanationEn: Setting the transformed Hamiltonian $K = H + \frac{\partial S}{\partial t} = 0$ with $p_i = \frac{\partial S}{\partial q_i}$ yields the Hamilton-Jacobi equation $H(q, \partial S/\partial q, t) + \partial S/\partial t = 0$.

questions.questionTextEn: The radiation pressure exerted by a plane electromagnetic wave of average intensity $I$ incident normally on a PERFECTLY REFLECTING mirror is:
questions.explanationEn: Total absorption transfers momentum flux $I/c$; perfect reflection reverses the photon momentum, doubling the radiation pressure to $2I/c$.

questions.questionTextEn: In quantum scattering theory, the Optical Theorem relates the total scattering cross-section $\sigma_{\text{tot}}$ to the forward scattering amplitude $f(0)$ by:
questions.explanationEn: Conservation of probability flux yields the Optical Theorem: $\sigma_{\text{tot}} = \frac{4\pi}{k}\,\text{Im}\,f(\theta = 0)$.

questions.questionTextEn: During a first-order phase transition (such as melting of ice at constant $T$ and $P$), which of the following quantities undergoes a DISCONTINUOUS jump?
questions.explanationEn: In a first-order phase transition, $G$ and $\mu$ are continuous across the phase boundary, while their first derivatives $S = -(\partial G/\partial T)_P$ and $V = (\partial G/\partial P)_T$ jump discontinuously (giving latent heat $L = T\Delta S$).

questions.questionTextEn: In the Normal Zeeman effect (for singlet states with $S = 0$), a spectral line splits in a uniform magnetic field into how many components when viewed perpendicular to the field?
questions.explanationEn: For $S = 0$, $g_J = 1$ for both levels, so all $\Delta M_L = 0$ transitions have the unshifted frequency $\nu_0$, while $\Delta M_L = \pm 1$ give $\nu_0 \pm \frac{eB}{4\pi m}$ — a Lorentz triplet of 3 lines.

questions.questionTextEn: For a 1D diatomic chain with 2 distinct atoms per primitive unit cell, how many acoustic and optical phonon branches exist?
questions.explanationEn: In $d$ dimensions with $p$ atoms per primitive cell, there are $d$ acoustic branches and $d(p - 1)$ optical branches. For $d = 1, p = 2$: 1 acoustic + 1 optical.

questions.questionTextEn: What is the Boolean simplification of $Y = (A + B)(A + B')$?
questions.explanationEn: Expanding: $A + AB' + AB + BB' = A(1 + B' + B) + 0 = A$.

questions.questionTextEn: In a nuclear gamma transition from a $2^+$ state to a $0^+$ ground state, the ONLY allowed electromagnetic multipole radiation is:
questions.explanationEn: Angular momentum selection gives $|2 - 0| \le L \le 2 + 0 \implies L = 2$. Since there is no parity change ($\pi_i \pi_f = +1$), the parity rule for electric multipoles $(-1)^L = (-1)^2 = +1$ selects pure $E2$.

questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following statements about a Hermitian matrix $H$ ($H^\dagger = H$) are ALWAYS TRUE?
optionsEn: Eigenvectors corresponding to distinct eigenvalues are mutually orthogonal
The determinant of $H$ is always positive
questions.explanationEn: Hermitian matrices have real eigenvalues (A), orthogonal eigenvectors for distinct eigenvalues (B), and generate unitary operators via $U = e^{iH}$ (C). Their determinant is real, not necessarily positive (e.g. Pauli matrices have $\det = -1$), so D is false.

questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following statements about a rigid body's principal moments of inertia $I_1, I_2, I_3$ are ALWAYS TRUE for any 3D rigid body?
optionsEn: All principal moments of inertia are non-negative
For a planar lamina lying in the $xy$-plane, $I_z = I_x + I_y$
The principal axes are always mutually orthogonal
questions.explanationEn: Since $I_1 = \sum m(y^2+z^2)$, $I_1 + I_2 = I_3 + 2\sum m z^2 \ge I_3$ (A), with equality for a planar lamina ($z=0$, perpendicular axis theorem C). Since $I_{ij}$ is real symmetric and positive semi-definite, B and D also hold.

questions.questionTextEn: Consider an oscillating electric dipole $\mathbf{p}(t) = p_0 \cos(\omega t)\hat{z}$. In the far-field radiation zone, which of the following statements are TRUE?
optionsEn: No power is radiated along the dipole axis ($\theta = 0$ and $\theta = \pi$)
Maximum radiated intensity occurs in the equatorial plane ($\theta = \pi/2$)
The total time-averaged radiated power scales as $\omega^4$
The radiation fields $\mathbf{E}$ and $\mathbf{B}$ fall off as $1/r^2$
questions.explanationEn: Dipole radiation pattern scales as $\sin^2\theta$ (zero on axis A, maximum at equator B) and total power $P = \frac{\mu_0 p_0^2 \omega^4}{12\pi c} \propto \omega^4$ (C). Radiation fields fall off as $1/r$, not $1/r^2$ (D is false).

questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following pairs of operators COMMUTE with each other?
optionsEn: $\hat{H}$ and $\hat{L}_z$ for any spherically symmetric potential $V(r)$
questions.explanationEn: $[\hat{L}^2, \hat{L}_z] = 0$ (A), different Cartesian components commute $[\hat{x}, \hat{p}_y] = 0$ (C), and rotational invariance gives $[\hat{H}, \hat{L}_z] = 0$ (D). $[\hat{L}_x, \hat{L}_y] = i\hbar\hat{L}_z \neq 0$ (B is false).

questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following statements about the 2D square-lattice Ising model (zero field) solved by Onsager are TRUE?
optionsEn: Near $T_c$, the specific heat diverges logarithmically ($\alpha = 0$)
The spontaneous magnetization vanishes as $(T_c - T)^{1/8}$ as $T \to T_c^-$
It exhibits a continuous (second-order) ferromagnetic phase transition at a finite critical temperature $T_c$
Mean-field theory predicts the exact critical exponents of the 2D Ising model
questions.explanationEn: Onsager's exact 2D solution gives finite $T_c$, logarithmic $C_V$ divergence, and $\beta = 1/8$ (A, B, C). Mean-field theory predicts $\beta = 1/2$ and a finite jump in $C_V$, which fails in 2D (D is false).

questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following statements about Raman scattering from a molecular sample at thermal equilibrium are TRUE?
optionsEn: Stokes lines have lower frequency than the incident laser light (molecule gains energy)
Anti-Stokes lines have higher frequency than the incident laser light (molecule loses energy)
The ratio of anti-Stokes to Stokes intensity decreases as temperature increases
At room temperature, Stokes lines are more intense than the corresponding anti-Stokes lines because the ground state is more populated than excited states
questions.explanationEn: A, B, and C are exact. Raising temperature increases excited-state population via $e^{-\Delta E / (k_B T)}$, so anti-Stokes/Stokes intensity ratio INCREASES with temperature (D is false).

questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following statements about negative feedback topologies in amplifiers are TRUE?
optionsEn: Negative feedback always increases the voltage gain
Voltage-shunt feedback decreases both input impedance and output impedance
Voltage-series feedback increases input impedance and decreases output impedance
Current-series feedback increases both input impedance and output impedance
questions.explanationEn: Series mixing raises $Z_{\text{in}}$; shunt mixing lowers $Z_{\text{in}}$; voltage sampling lowers $Z_{\text{out}}$; current sampling raises $Z_{\text{out}}$ (A, B, C true). Negative feedback reduces gain (D false).

questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following conservation laws are violated in weak interactions?
questions.explanationEn: Weak interactions violate $P$, $C$, $S$ (in charged-current quark transitions), and even $CP$ in kaon/B-meson systems, whereas electric charge $Q$ is strictly conserved.

questions.questionTextEn: What is the largest eigenvalue of the matrix $\begin{pmatrix} 4 & 2 \\ 2 & 1 \end{pmatrix}$?
questions.explanationEn: Trace = 5 and determinant = $4 - 4 = 0$, so the characteristic equation is $\lambda^2 - 5\lambda = 0$, giving eigenvalues 0 and 5.

questions.questionTextEn: A planet's semi-major axis around a star is 4 AU. If a planet at 1 AU has an orbital period of 1 year, what is the orbital period (in years) of the planet at 4 AU?
questions.explanationEn: By Kepler's third law $T^2 \propto a^3$: $T = 4^{3/2} = 8$ years.

questions.questionTextEn: Light travels from glass ($n_1 = 1.5$) toward air ($n_2 = 1.0$). What is the sine of the critical angle for total internal reflection? (Round to 2 decimal places.)
What is the eigenvalue of $\hat{L}^2$ (in units of $\hbar^2$) for an electron in a $d$-orbital ($l = 2$)?
questions.explanationEn: $\hat{L}^2 |l, m\rangle = l(l+1)\hbar^2 |l, m\rangle$. For $l = 2$, $2(3) = 6$.

questions.questionTextEn: In a 3D ideal classical gas of $N$ particles, if the particle density $n$ is held constant and the temperature $T$ is quadrupled, by what factor does the thermal de Broglie wavelength $\lambda_T = h / \sqrt{2\pi m k_B T}$ change?
questions.explanationEn: $\lambda_T \propto T^{-1/2}$, so quadrupling $T$ halves $\lambda_T$ (factor $0.5$).

questions.questionTextEn: For a rigid diatomic molecule with rotational constant $B = 2\text{ cm}^{-1}$, what is the wavenumber (in $\text{cm}^{-1}$) of the pure rotational absorption line for the transition $J = 2 \to J = 3$?
In a 1D tight-binding band $E(k) = E_0 - 2t\cos(ka)$ with hopping integral $t = 1.5\text{ eV}$, what is the total energy bandwidth $W = E_{\max} - E_{\min}$ (in eV)?
questions.explanationEn: $E_{\min} = E_0 - 2t$ and $E_{\max} = E_0 + 2t$, so bandwidth $W = 4t = 4(1.5) = 6\text{ eV}$.

questions.questionTextEn: Convert the binary number $(11011)_2$ to decimal.
The inverse Laplace transform of $F(s) = \frac{2s + 5}{s^2 + 4s + 13}$ is:
Consider a 1D particle of mass $m$ in a uniform gravitational field with Hamiltonian $H = \frac{p^2}{2m} + mgz$. What is the value of the Poisson bracket $[z, H]$?
questions.explanationEn: $[z, H] = \frac{\partial H}{\partial p} = \frac{p}{m} = \dot{z}$.

questions.questionTextEn: A solid non-conducting sphere of radius $R$ carries a spherically symmetric volume charge density $\rho(r) = k r$ ($k$ constant). What is the electric field magnitude $E(r)$ inside the sphere ($r < R$)?
questions.explanationEn: Enclosed charge $Q(r) = \int_0^r (k r')(4\pi r'^2 dr') = \pi k r^4$. By Gauss's law, $E(4\pi r^2) = \frac{\pi k r^4}{\varepsilon_0} \implies E(r) = \frac{k r^2}{4\varepsilon_0}$.

questions.questionTextEn: In the Schrödinger picture vs. Heisenberg picture of quantum mechanics:
optionsEn: In the Schrödinger picture, operators carry all time dependence
In the Heisenberg picture, operators evolve in time while state vectors remain fixed
Expectation values of observables differ between the two pictures
The two pictures are equivalent only for free particles
questions.explanationEn: In the Schrödinger picture states evolve ($|\psi(t)\rangle = U(t)|\psi(0)\rangle$); in the Heisenberg picture operators evolve ($A_H(t) = U^\dagger A_S U$) while states stay fixed, yielding identical expectation values.

questions.questionTextEn: A classical ultra-relativistic gas of $N$ non-interacting particles with dispersion $\epsilon = c|\mathbf{p}|$ is enclosed in a 3D volume $V$ at temperature $T$. What is its molar heat capacity at constant volume $C_V$ and adiabatic index $\gamma = C_P / C_V$?
questions.explanationEn: Single-particle partition function $z = \frac{V}{h^3}\int_0^\infty 4\pi p^2 e^{-\beta cp}dp = 8\pi V \left(\frac{k_B T}{hc}\right)^3 \propto T^3$. Thus $U = 3 N k_B T \implies C_V = 3R$, $C_P = C_V + R = 4R$, and $\gamma = 4/3$.

questions.questionTextEn: In a rovibrational infrared spectrum of a rigid diatomic molecule (rotational constant $B$), what is the frequency gap between the first line of the R-branch ($J = 0 \to 1$) and the first line of the P-branch ($J = 1 \to 0$)?
questions.explanationEn: $R(0) = \bar{\nu}_0 + 2B$ and $P(1) = \bar{\nu}_0 - 2B$, so the gap across the missing band origin (Q-branch) is $4B$.

questions.questionTextEn: For an FCC crystal of lattice constant $a$, what is the ratio of the first two allowed Bragg peak $\sin^2\theta$ values in powder X-ray diffraction?
questions.explanationEn: The lowest allowed $(hkl)$ planes in FCC (all odd or all even) are $(111)$ with $h^2+k^2+l^2 = 3$ and $(200)$ with $h^2+k^2+l^2 = 4$. Since $\sin^2\theta \propto h^2+k^2+l^2$, the ratio is $3 : 4$.

questions.questionTextEn: In $\beta^+$ decay of a nucleus $^A_Z X \to {}^A_{Z-1} Y + e^+ + \nu_e$, the condition for the decay to be energetically possible in terms of neutral atomic masses $M(A,Z)$ and $M(A,Z-1)$ is:
questions.explanationEn: Expressing nuclear masses via atomic masses ($M_{\text{nuc}} = M_{\text{atom}} - Z m_e$), $Q_{\beta^+} = [M(A,Z) - Z m_e - (M(A,Z-1) - (Z-1)m_e) - m_e]c^2 = [M(A,Z) - M(A,Z-1) - 2m_e]c^2 > 0$.

questions.questionTextEn: Consider the complex function $f(z) = \frac{1}{z(z - 2)^2}$. Which of the following statements are TRUE?
optionsEn: $z = 0$ is a simple pole with residue $1/4$
$z = 2$ is a pole of order 2 with residue $-1/4$
questions.explanationEn: $\text{Res}(0) = 1/(-2)^2 = 1/4$ (A). $\text{Res}(2) = \left.\frac{d}{dz}(1/z)\right|_{z=2} = -1/4$ (B). Sum of residues inside $|z|=3$ is $1/4 - 1/4 = 0$, so the integral vanishes (C). Since $f(1/w) = w^3/(1-2w)^2$ is analytic at $w=0$, $z=\infty$ is removable, not essential (D is false).

questions.questionTextEn: For an ideal magnetic material with relative permeability $\mu_r = 1 + \chi_m$, which of the following statements are TRUE?
optionsEn: The bound volume current density is $\mathbf{J}_b = \nabla \cdot \mathbf{M}$
For a paramagnetic material, $\chi_m > 0$ and small
Inside a Type-I superconductor in the Meissner state, $\chi_m = -1$ (perfect diamagnetism)
questions.explanationEn: A, B, and C are exact. Bound volume current is $\mathbf{J}_b = \nabla \times \mathbf{M}$ (curl, not divergence), so D is false.

questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following statements about the Einstein and Debye models of lattice specific heat are TRUE?
optionsEn: The Debye model correctly predicts $C_V \propto T^3$ at low $T$ in 3D solids
The Debye model treats all phonon modes as having the exact same frequency $\omega_D$
Both models reproduce the classical Dulong-Petit limit $C_V \to 3R$ at high temperatures ($T \gg \Theta$)
The Einstein model predicts an exponential drop $C_V \propto e^{-\Theta_E/T}$ at low $T$, which underestimates experimental values
questions.explanationEn: A, B, and C are exact. Treating all modes at a single frequency is the EINSTEIN model, not the Debye model (D is false).

questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following statements about BJT biasing and stability factor $S = \frac{\partial I_C}{\partial I_{CBO}}$ are TRUE?
optionsEn: Adding an emitter resistor $R_E$ introduces positive DC feedback
For fixed bias, $S = 1 + \beta$ (very poor thermal stability)
Voltage-divider bias with an emitter resistor $R_E$ provides significantly better thermal stability (smaller $S$) than simple fixed base bias
The ideal minimum value of stability factor $S$ is $1$
questions.explanationEn: Voltage-divider bias with $R_E$ introduces NEGATIVE DC feedback (D is false) that reduces $S$ close to its ideal minimum of 1 (A, C true), whereas fixed bias gives $S = 1 + \beta$ (B true).

questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following statements about the four fundamental interactions are CORRECT?
optionsEn: The weak interaction has an infinite range
Photons do not self-interact directly at tree level because they carry no electric charge
$W^\pm$ bosons self-interact with photons and $Z^0$ bosons because the electroweak gauge group $SU(2)_L \times U(1)_Y$ is non-Abelian
Gluons self-interact because they carry color charge
questions.explanationEn: QED is Abelian (no tree-level photon self-coupling), whereas QCD and $SU(2)_L$ are non-Abelian (gluon and $W/Z$ self-couplings). Because $W^\pm, Z^0$ are heavy ($80$–$91\text{ GeV}$), the weak interaction is very short-ranged ($\sim 10^{-18}\text{ m}$).

questions.questionTextEn: If $A$ and $B$ are $2 \times 2$ matrices such that $\text{Tr}(A) = 4, \det(A) = 3$, what is $\text{Tr}(A^{-1})$? (Round to 2 decimal places.)
questions.explanationEn: If eigenvalues of $A$ are $\lambda_1, \lambda_2$, then $\text{Tr}(A^{-1}) = \frac{1}{\lambda_1} + \frac{1}{\lambda_2} = \frac{\lambda_1 + \lambda_2}{\lambda_1\lambda_2} = \frac{\text{Tr}(A)}{\det(A)} = \frac{4}{3} \approx 1.33$.

questions.questionTextEn: What is the value of the definite integral $\int_0^{\pi/2} \sin^3\theta \cos^3\theta\,d\theta$ multiplied by 12?
questions.explanationEn: Using $\int_0^{\pi/2} \sin^{2m-1}\theta \cos^{2n-1}\theta\,d\theta = \frac{1}{2}B(m, n)$ with $m = 2, n = 2$: $\frac{1}{2} \cdot \frac{\Gamma(2)\Gamma(2)}{\Gamma(4)} = \frac{1}{2} \cdot \frac{1}{6} = \frac{1}{12}$. Multiplying by 12 gives 1.

questions.questionTextEn: A proton (rest energy $\approx 938\text{ MeV}$) collides with a stationary proton to produce a proton-antiproton pair: $p + p \to p + p + p + \bar{p}$. What is the threshold kinetic energy of the incident proton in units of the proton rest energy $m_p c^2$?
questions.explanationEn: In CM frame, minimum invariant mass is $4m_p c^2$. In lab frame: $(E_1 + m_p c^2)^2 - (p_1 c)^2 = 16 m_p^2 c^4 \implies 2m_p^2 c^4 + 2 E_1 m_p c^2 = 16 m_p^2 c^4 \implies E_1 = 7 m_p c^2$. Threshold kinetic energy $K = E_1 - m_p c^2 = 6 m_p c^2$.

questions.questionTextEn: A 1D particle with Hamiltonian $H(q, p) = \frac{p^2}{2} + \frac{1}{2}q^2$ starts at $q(0) = 3, p(0) = 4$. What is its maximum displacement $q_{\max}$ during the motion?
questions.explanationEn: Total energy $E = \frac{4^2}{2} + \frac{3^2}{2} = \frac{25}{2}$. At maximum displacement $p = 0$, so $\frac{1}{2}q_{\max}^2 = \frac{25}{2} \implies q_{\max} = 5$.

questions.questionTextEn: A uniform sphere of radius $R$ carries total charge $Q$ distributed uniformly throughout its volume. Its electrostatic self-energy is $U = k \frac{Q^2}{4\pi\varepsilon_0 R}$. What is the exact value of $k$?
questions.explanationEn: Integrating $\frac{1}{2}\varepsilon_0 E^2$ over inside ($r < R$) and outside ($r > R$) gives $U = \frac{3}{5}\frac{Q^2}{4\pi\varepsilon_0 R}$, so $k = 3/5 = 0.6$.

questions.questionTextEn: An electron in a uniform magnetic field $B = 0.1\text{ T}$ executes non-relativistic circular cyclotron motion. Taking $e/m = 1.76 \times 10^{11}\text{ C/kg}$, what is its cyclotron frequency $f_c = \frac{eB}{2\pi m}$ (in GHz, rounded to 2 decimal places)?
questions.explanationEn: $f_c = \frac{1.76 \times 10^{11} \times 0.1}{2\pi} \approx 2.801 \times 10^9\text{ Hz} = 2.80\text{ GHz}$.

questions.questionTextEn: A 1D particle is in the $n = 2$ state of a harmonic oscillator. What is the value of $\frac{\Delta x \cdot \Delta p_x}{\hbar}$ for this state?
questions.explanationEn: For a 1D harmonic oscillator eigenstate $|n\rangle$, $\Delta x \cdot \Delta p_x = \left(n + \frac{1}{2}\right)\hbar$. For $n = 2$, this is $2.5\hbar$.

questions.questionTextEn: In a 1D attractive delta well $V(x) = -\alpha\,\delta(x)$, if $\alpha$ is tripled to $3\alpha$, by what factor does the magnitude of the bound-state binding energy $|E|$ increase?
questions.explanationEn: $|E| = \frac{m\alpha^2}{2\hbar^2} \propto \alpha^2$. Tripling $\alpha$ multiplies $|E|$ by $3^2 = 9$.

questions.questionTextEn: In the WKB approximation for a 1D quartic oscillator $V(x) = \alpha x^4$, the energy scales as $E_n \propto (n + 1/2)^p$. What is the exponent $p$? (Round to 2 decimal places.)
questions.explanationEn: For $V(x) \propto |x|^k$, WKB gives $E_n \propto (n + 1/2)^{\frac{2k}{k+2}}$. For $k = 4$, $p = \frac{8}{6} = \frac{4}{3} \approx 1.33$.

questions.questionTextEn: An ideal gas undergoes a polytropic process $P V^{1.5} = \text{constant}$. If its volume increases by a factor of 4, by what factor does its absolute temperature $T$ change?
A system of $N = 100$ independent spins ($s_i = \pm 1$) has magnetization $M = \sum s_i$ with zero field. What is the root-mean-square fluctuation $\sqrt{\langle M^2 \rangle}$?
questions.explanationEn: $\langle M^2 \rangle = \sum_{i=1}^N \langle s_i^2 \rangle = N = 100 \implies \sqrt{\langle M^2 \rangle} = 10$.

questions.questionTextEn: For an atomic transition between $^1 D_2$ and $^1 P_1$ in a weak magnetic field (Normal Zeeman effect), how many total allowed $\Delta M_L = 0, \pm 1$ transitions exist (counting all individual $M_L \to M_L'$ pairs before noting frequency degeneracy)?
questions.explanationEn: Lower level $^1 P_1$ has $M_L' = -1, 0, +1$. Each $M_L'$ receives 3 allowed transitions from $^1 D_2$ ($M_L = M_L' - 1, M_L', M_L' + 1$), giving $3 \times 3 = 9$ individual transitions (collapsing to 3 distinct frequencies).

questions.questionTextEn: A laser beam has a Gaussian waist radius $w_0 = 1\text{ mm}$ at wavelength $\lambda = 628\text{ nm}$. What is its far-field half-angle divergence $\theta = \frac{\lambda}{\pi w_0}$ (in milliradians)?
questions.explanationEn: $\theta = \frac{628 \times 10^{-9}}{3.1416 \times 10^{-3}} \approx 2.0 \times 10^{-4}\text{ rad} = 0.2\text{ mrad}$.

questions.questionTextEn: An intrinsic semiconductor has band gap $E_g = 0.8\text{ eV}$. Taking $k_B = 8.617 \times 10^{-5}\text{ eV/K}$, by approximately what factor does $e^{-E_g/(2k_B T)}$ increase when temperature increases from $300\text{ K}$ to $400\text{ K}$? (Round to 1 decimal place.)
questions.explanationEn: Exponent difference $\frac{E_g}{2k_B}\left(\frac{1}{300} - \frac{1}{400}\right) = \frac{0.4}{8.617 \times 10^{-5}} \cdot \frac{1}{1200} = 3.868$. Factor = $e^{3.868} \approx 47.86 \approx 47.9$.

questions.questionTextEn: A simple cubic crystal has lattice constant $a = 2\,\text{\AA}$. What is the magnitude of the shortest non-zero reciprocal lattice vector $|\mathbf{G}| = 2\pi/a$ (in $\text{\AA}^{-1}$, rounded to 2 decimal places)?
questions.explanationEn: $|\mathbf{G}| = 2\pi / 2 = \pi \approx 3.14\,\text{\AA}^{-1}$.

questions.questionTextEn: A sinusoidal voltage has an RMS value of $10\text{ V}$. What is its peak-to-peak voltage $V_{\text{pp}}$ (in Volts, rounded to 1 decimal place)?
questions.explanationEn: $V_{\text{pp}} = 2\sqrt{2} V_{\text{rms}} = 2.8284 \times 10 \approx 28.3\text{ V}$.

questions.questionTextEn: $^{226}\text{Ra}$ undergoes $\alpha$-decay to $^{222}\text{Rn}$ with a $Q$-value of $4.87\text{ MeV}$. The recoil kinetic energy of the $^{222}\text{Rn}$ daughter nucleus (in $\text{keV}$) is ________. (rounded off to one decimal place)
questions.explanationEn: $T_D = \frac{4}{226} Q = \frac{4}{226} \times 4870\text{ keV} = 86.19\text{ keV} \approx 86.2\text{ keV}$.
